ffmpeg.help.ff_v_profile: A balanced set of size/quality tuned parameters. Choose Custom to tweak each option.
ffmpeg.help.ff_v_encoder: Codec used to re-encode video. auto picks one based on the output container. H.264 is most compatible; H.265/AV1 are smaller; NVENC uses the GPU.
ffmpeg.help.ff_v_crf: Constant quality factor: lower = better quality & larger file (18≈visually lossless, 23 default, 28 smaller). Equivalent levels differ per codec and are converted automatically.
ffmpeg.help.ff_v_preset: Trade-off between encode speed and compression. Slower yields smaller files but takes longer.
ffmpeg.help.ff_v_tune: Tune encoding to the content (live action / animation / film grain, etc.). Keep default for live action; animation/screencast can save more with animation.
ffmpeg.help.ff_v_maxwidth: Scale video width to at most this value (0 = no scaling). Aspect ratio is kept.
ffmpeg.help.ff_v_fps: Set frame rate (0 = keep original). Lowering FPS shrinks size noticeably.
ffmpeg.help.ff_v_audio: How to handle the audio track: auto follows the video codec, copy keeps it as-is, none removes audio.
ffmpeg.help.ff_v_pixfmt: Pixel sampling format. yuv420p works on all players and browsers; keep retains the source format (may not play on some devices).
ffmpeg.help.ff_v_abr: Target audio bitrate in kbps. Used only when audio is aac/libopus.
ffmpeg.help.ff_v_faststart: Moves the index to the file head for progressive web playback. Recommended for web sharing.
ffmpeg.help.ff_a_profile: A balanced set of size/quality tuned parameters. Choose Custom to tweak each option.
ffmpeg.help.ff_a_encoder: Codec used to re-encode audio. Opus is small with good quality, AAC is most compatible, MP3 is universal, FLAC is lossless.
ffmpeg.help.ff_a_bitrate: Target bitrate in kbps. Higher = better quality & larger file.
ffmpeg.help.ff_a_mp3q: MP3 variable-bitrate quality: 0 best, 9 smallest. 2 is roughly transparent (recommended).
ffmpeg.help.ff_a_flac_level: FLAC lossless compression level (0-12). Higher = smaller but slower.
ffmpeg.help.ff_a_samplerate: Output sample rate in Hz. Lowering reduces size but loses high frequencies.
ffmpeg.help.ff_i_profile: A balanced set of size/quality tuned parameters. Choose Custom to tweak each option.
ffmpeg.help.ff_i_encoder: Codec used to re-encode the image. WebP is small and universal, AVIF is smaller, MJPEG/PNG are most compatible.
ffmpeg.help.ff_i_quality: Lossy quality (1-100), used for WebP/MJPEG. Higher = sharper.
ffmpeg.help.ff_i_crf: Constant quality factor (0-63), used for AVIF. Lower = better quality.
ffmpeg.help.ff_i_effort: AV1 encode effort (0-6). Higher = smaller but slower.
ffmpeg.help.ff_i_maxwidth: Scale image width to at most this value (0 = no scaling). Aspect ratio is kept.

advanced.help.backend: Compression engine. Auto picks by format; oxipng is PNG-only; jpegoptim is JPG/JPEG-only; Pillow is the universal fallback. If the selected tool is unavailable the job falls back to Pillow automatically.
advanced.help.interlace: Interlace: image loads progressively on web.
advanced.help.strip: Strip metadata: safe=keep color info, all=remove everything.
advanced.help.merge: Merge: combine output files into one.
compress.label: compressed
advanced.help.alpha: Alpha optimize: optimize transparency channel compression
advanced.help.optimize: Huffman table optimization: reduces JPEG size by ~5-10%
advanced.compression.route: Auto mode: PNG -> oxipng, JPG/JPEG -> jpegoptim, others -> Pillow.
advanced.help.jo.mode: Lossless only rebuilds the Huffman tables - pixels stay identical. Lossy re-encodes at the quality cap for a smaller file.
advanced.help.jo.max: Maximum quality factor (0-100) in lossy mode. 85 is usually visually identical; around 70 shrinks files noticeably.
advanced.help.jo.strip: Strip embedded metadata. Removing the ICC profile can shift colours - use with care.
advanced.help.jo.prog: Progressive JPEGs fade in while loading and are usually smaller. Auto keeps whichever variant is smaller.
advanced.help.jo.threshold: Keep the original file when the gain is below this percentage. 0 disables the threshold.
advanced.help.jo.retry: Optimise repeatedly until the size stops changing. Slightly smaller output, noticeably slower.
advanced.help.pil.quality: Compression quality: 0 worst, 95 best. Pillow advises against going above 95 - the file grows fast for almost no visual gain.
advanced.help.pil.optimize: Runs an extra encoding pass to pick better coding tables. Smaller files, slightly slower.
advanced.help.pil.progressive: Produce a progressive JPEG: fades in while loading and is usually smaller.
advanced.help.pil.subsampling: Controls how much colour information is kept. 4:4:4 keeps everything (largest); 4:2:0 compresses hardest and can blur red edges.
engine.card.title: Upscaling & Interpolation Engines
engine.card.hint: Engines are not bundled with the app. Use "Download page" to get the archive, extract it into tools/<engine-id>, then hit "Rescan".
engine.desc.realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan: General-purpose real-world upscaler for both photos and artwork. The official archive ships 4 models; Vulkan runs on any modern GPU.
engine.desc.waifu2x-ncnn-vulkan: The classic anime upscaler with independent denoise and scale control. CUnet gives the best quality, UpConv7 is faster; up to 32x.
engine.desc.waifu2x-caffe: The long-standing Windows Waifu2x build (waifu2x-caffe-cui.exe). Widest model selection, but requires an NVIDIA GPU with cuDNN.
engine.desc.waifu2x-converter: OpenCV/OpenCL Waifu2x port. Runs on CPU-only machines and accepts arbitrary fractional scale ratios.
engine.desc.srmd-ncnn-vulkan: General upscaler with a 0–10 continuous denoise dial. Great for noisy or slightly blurred legacy footage, slower than Real-ESRGAN.
engine.desc.srmd-cuda: CUDA build of SRMD. NVIDIA-only, faster than the Vulkan build at the same settings, requires a working CUDA runtime.
engine.desc.realsr-ncnn-vulkan: 4x upscaler trained on real-world photo degradation. The DF2K_JPEG model tolerates JPEG artifacts well.
engine.desc.realcugan-ncnn-vulkan: Modern anime upscaler that preserves more detail than Waifu2x. 1–4x scale, -1–3 denoise; sync-gap removes tile seams.
engine.desc.anime4kcpp: Ships both Anime4K (ultra-fast sharpening pipeline, real-time capable) and ACNet (CNN-based, higher quality). HDN adds strong denoising.
engine.desc.rtx-super-resolution: NVIDIA driver-level video super resolution (RTX 20-series or newer). It has no standalone CLI; drop the Maxine Video Effects SDK sample (UpscalePipelineApp.exe) into this folder to use it.
engine.desc.rife-ncnn-vulkan: The fastest and most reliable real-time interpolator. v4.6 is the best all-rounder; enable UHD mode for 4K+ sources.
engine.desc.cain-ncnn-vulkan: Channel-attention interpolation with fewer ghosting artifacts on large anime motion. Fixed 2x steps only.
engine.desc.dain-ncnn-vulkan: Depth-aware interpolation with the best occlusion handling and quality, but far heavier on VRAM and time than RIFE. Use tiling.
engine.desc.ifrnet-ncnn-vulkan: Lightweight, efficient interpolation with a good speed/quality balance. Vimeo90K is general purpose; GoPro suits fast motion.
upscale.engine.none: No model / algorithm available, please download
upscale.engine.none_hint: No super-resolution or interpolation engine detected. Open the About page to see every supported engine, then drop it into its tools folder.
engine.reason.cuda: Requires the NVIDIA CUDA toolkit; one-click download is unsupported. Install manually into the tools/ folder.
engine.reason.driver: Built into the NVIDIA display driver (Maxine); no download needed — enable it in the driver / control panel.
engine.reason.platform: One-click download is unavailable on this platform; get the matching build from the official site and place it in the tools/ folder.
engine.help.model: Select the model / algorithm weights file to use.
engine.help.tile: Tile size; 0 = auto. Larger uses more VRAM, smaller is slower.
engine.help.gpu: Inference device: auto picks an available GPU; cpu uses the processor only.
engine.help.tta: Test-time augmentation: slightly better quality but much slower.
engine.help.jobs: Thread/process allocation (a:b:c); auto adapts to hardware.
engine.help.multiplier: Interpolation factor: multiplies the source frame rate (2x = one new frame between every two).
engine.help.mode: Processing mode: upscale only / denoise only / both.
engine.help.crop_size: Crop size for tiled processing to avoid running out of VRAM.
engine.help.block_size: Block size; 0 = auto. Larger is faster but uses more VRAM.
engine.help.gpu_off: Disable GPU acceleration and use the CPU (slower but more compatible).
engine.help.passes: Number of passes; more passes improve quality but slow things down.
engine.help.push_color: Color push count (1–4); more pushes make colors richer.
engine.help.gpu_on: Enable GPU acceleration (off uses the CPU).
engine.help.uhd: Enable UHD mode for better quality on large resolutions.
engine.help.tta_temporal: Temporal TTA: joint cross-frame enhancement for steadier video.
engine.help.syncgap: Frame-alignment sync-gap parameter affecting multi-frame alignment.
